tools.name: analyze_csharp_code_style
tools.description: Runs the core C# code-quality checks on a single source file and returns one combined report: coding style, member ordering, naming conventions, async/await patterns, and nullable safety. Use this whenever generating, editing, or reviewing C# code. Pass the source as content and, when available, the file's absolute path as filePath so the effective .editorconfig style rules can be resolved and applied. For project-structure rules use analyze_csharp_project_structure; for test-specific rules use analyze_csharp_testing_style.

content.description: The C# source code to check.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the file whose source is in content. Used to resolve the effective .editorconfig style rules that apply to the file.

tools.name: analyze_csharp_project_structure
tools.description: Checks a single C# source file for project-structure rules: file-scoped namespaces, one type per file, the file name matching the type name, and no '#pragma warning disable'. Pass the source as content and the file's absolute path as filePath (used to compare the file name against the declared type name).

content.description: The C# source code to check.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the file whose source is in content. Used to check the file name against the declared type name.

tools.name: analyze_csharp_testing_style
tools.description: Checks a single C# test file for test conventions: test class and method naming, no XML doc comments, Assert.Multiple for multi-assertion tests, no ConfigureAwait, and namespace conformance (RootNamespace + folder path within the project). Use this when generating, editing, or reviewing C# test files. Pass the test source as content and the test file's absolute path as filePath (used for the file-name and namespace checks). Also pass projectDirectory (absolute path of the test project's directory) and optionally rootNamespace so the namespace rule can verify the namespace matches RootNamespace + folder path.

content.description: The C# test source code to check.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the test file whose source is in content. Used by the file-name and namespace checks.

projectDirectory.description: Absolute path of the test project's directory (the folder containing the .csproj). Used to compute the expected namespace from RootNamespace + the file's folder path within the project.

rootNamespace.description: The test project's RootNamespace (e.g. 'MyApp.Tests'). When omitted, falls back to the filename (without extension) of the first *.csproj found in projectDirectory, matching MSBuild's default behaviour.

tools.name: analyze_nuget_references
tools.description: Inspects a .csproj file's PackageReference entries for hygiene issues: duplicate references, floating or wildcard versions (e.g. '*' or version ranges), missing Version attributes (unless Central Package Management is enabled via ManagePackageVersionsCentrally), and packages that have a built-in .NET equivalent. Use this whenever adding, updating, or reviewing NuGet dependencies. Pass the full .csproj XML as content.

content.description: The full XML content of the .csproj file to inspect.

tools.name: analyze_git_commit_message
tools.description: Validates a Git commit message against project conventions. Covers Conventional Commits format (type, scope, subject, line lengths) and content best practices (no anti-patterns in the body). Use this before creating any commit. Pass the full message — subject and body — as content.

content.description: The full commit message to validate.

tools.name: read_editorconfig_rules
tools.description: Resolves the effective .editorconfig properties for a single file by walking up the directory tree, evaluating glob patterns, and applying section cascading. Returns the final flat key/value map that applies to that file. Use this when you need to know the coding-style rules (indent style, charset, end-of-line, language-specific keys) in force at a particular file path. Pass the file's absolute path as filePath.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file whose effective .editorconfig properties should be resolved.

tools.name: analyze_typescript_code_style
tools.description: Runs every enabled TypeScript code-quality check on a single source file and returns one combined report. Flags anti-patterns including any, enums, @ts-ignore, type assertions, non-null assertions, unconstrained generics, and the Function/Object/{} types. Use this whenever generating, editing, or reviewing TypeScript code. Pass the source as content.

content.description: The TypeScript source code to check.
